fields.CONTENT: QTSPs SHALL RECORD all relevant information concerning data issued and received and SHALL KEEP it accessible EVEN AFTER THE ACTIVITIES HAVE CEASED for as long as necessary, in order to be able to provide evidence in LEGAL PROCEEDINGS and to ensure the CONTINUITY of the service. Such recording may be done electronically.
fields.PURPOSE: Without records the QTSP cannot exculpate itself under Article 13(1), third subparagraph – point (h) is the practical precondition of the reversal of the burden of proof.
fields.DEADLINE: 'for as long as necessary' – the specific duration follows from national law
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 13(1) · Liability and reversal of the burden of proof Trust service providers are liable for damage caused intentionally or negligently, expressly including non-material damage – an extension introduced by eIDAS 2.0. The decisive difference is set out in the second and third subparagraphs: with a non-qualified provider the injured party must prove intention or negligence, with a qualified provider both are presumed unless that provider exculpates itself. Only thereby does qualified status acquire a value in liability law. Article 46b(4) · Catalogue of tasks of the supervisory body Eleven tasks, among them notification of the NIS2 authorities, the ANALYSIS OF THE CONFORMITY ASSESSMENT REPORTS (point (c)), audits, cooperation with the data protection authorities, granting and withdrawal of qualified status, informing the body responsible for the trusted list, the VERIFICATION OF THE TERMINATION PLANS (point (i)) as well as the investigation of web-browser notifications under Article 45a (point (k)).
fields.AUDIT CHECK: For how long are records kept, and has the period been reconciled with national law and with the limitation periods?
fields.KEY POINT: Point (h) outlives the undertaking – the duty does not end with operations.

fields.CONTENT: QTSPs SHALL HAVE an UP-TO-DATE TERMINATION PLAN to ensure the continuity of the service in accordance with provisions that are verified by the supervisory body pursuant to Article 46b(4), point (i).
fields.PURPOSE: A certificate can remain valid longer than its issuer exists – the termination plan protects users against the failure of the provider. (Point (j) was deleted by eIDAS 2.0.)
fields.DEADLINE: to be kept up to date on an ongoing basis
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 46b(4) · Catalogue of tasks of the supervisory body Eleven tasks, among them notification of the NIS2 authorities, the ANALYSIS OF THE CONFORMITY ASSESSMENT REPORTS (point (c)), audits, cooperation with the data protection authorities, granting and withdrawal of qualified status, informing the body responsible for the trusted list, the VERIFICATION OF THE TERMINATION PLANS (point (i)) as well as the investigation of web-browser notifications under Article 45a (point (k)). Article 24(2) · Catalogue of QTSP obligations The central catalogue, in practice the structure of every audit: (a) notification duties (one month for changes, three months for cessation), (b) qualified and trained staff in accordance with European or international standards, (c) sufficient financial resources or liability insurance, (d) pre-contractual information, (e) trustworthy systems including suitable cryptographic techniques, (f) verifiable data storage, (fa) risk management, (fb) 24-hour notification, (g) protection against forgery and data loss, (h) recording duty extending beyond the cessation of activities, (i) termination plan, (k) certificate database. Point (j) was deleted – the gap is intentional.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: When was the termination plan last updated and verified by the supervisory body?
fields.KEY POINT: Mind the gap: point (i) is followed by point (k) – point (j) no longer exists.

fields.CONTENT: QTSPs issuing qualified certificates SHALL ESTABLISH a CERTIFICATE DATABASE and KEEP IT UPDATED.
fields.PURPOSE: Basis for revocation management and status enquiry – without an up-to-date database Article 24(3)/(4) cannot be complied with.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 24(3) · Revocation within 24 hours The QTSP registers the revocation in its certificate database and publishes the revocation status in a timely manner, in any event within 24 hours after RECEIPT OF THE REQUEST – not after its own decision. The revocation becomes effective only upon publication; an unpublished revocation protects no one. “publish the revocation status of the certificate in a timely manner, and in any event within 24 hours after the receipt of the request. The revocation shall become effective immediately upon its publication.” ✓ Article 24(3) eIDAS Article 24(4) · Permanent status information The QTSP makes information on the validity and revocation status available to relying parties – at least on a per certificate basis, at any time, beyond the validity period, in an automated manner, reliably, free of charge and efficiently. The addition 'beyond the validity period' is decisive: only in that way can signatures still be validated years later. Article 28(5) · Temporary suspension Allows the Member States to lay down national rules on the temporary suspension of qualified certificates under two conditions: the certificate loses its validity for the period of suspension, and the period of suspension is to be clearly indicated in the certificate database and the suspension status is to be made visible from the service providing information on the status of the certificate. Article 38(5) · Temporary suspension for seal certificates Allows national suspension rules under the same conditions as Article 28(5): loss of validity for the period of suspension and clear indication of the period in the certificate database as well as in the status service.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Is the certificate database complete, up to date and protected against unauthorised modification?
fields.KEY POINT: Applies only to certificate-issuing QTSPs – not, for example, to pure time-stamping services.

fields.CONTENT: If a QTSP decides to revoke a certificate, it SHALL REGISTER such revocation in its certificate database and SHALL PUBLISH the revocation status IN A TIMELY MANNER, IN ANY EVENT WITHIN 24 HOURS after the receipt of the request. The revocation SHALL BECOME EFFECTIVE IMMEDIATELY UPON ITS PUBLICATION.
fields.PURPOSE: An unpublished revocation protects no one – only publication produces effect.
fields.DEADLINE: 24 hours from receipt of the request
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 24(4) · Permanent status information The QTSP makes information on the validity and revocation status available to relying parties – at least on a per certificate basis, at any time, beyond the validity period, in an automated manner, reliably, free of charge and efficiently. The addition 'beyond the validity period' is decisive: only in that way can signatures still be validated years later. Article 24(4a) · Extension to attestations of attributes Provides that paragraphs 3 and 4 apply accordingly to the revocation of qualified electronic attestations of attributes. The 24-hour time limit and the permanent status information thus apply there as well. Article 28(4) · Finality of revocation A revoked qualified certificate loses its validity and its status shall not in any circumstances be reverted. A reversible intermediate stage exists only by way of the suspension under paragraph 5, the period of which must be visible in the certificate database. The same finality applies under Article 38(4), Article 45d(4) and Article 45f(4). Article 38(4) · Finality of revocation Provides that a revoked qualified certificate for electronic seal is no longer valid from the moment of its revocation and that its status shall not in any circumstances be reverted. Article 45d(4) · Finality of revocation Provides that a revoked qualified electronic attestation of attributes is no longer valid from the moment of its revocation and shall not in any circumstances regain validity.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Is the 24-hour time limit measured and evaluated? From what point does it start to run in the process?
fields.KEY POINT: 24 hours from the REQUEST, not from the decision. Effective upon publication.

fields.CONTENT: QTSPs SHALL PROVIDE relying parties (RP) with information on the VALIDITY OR REVOCATION STATUS – at least on a per certificate basis, AT ANY TIME, BEYOND THE VALIDITY PERIOD, in an AUTOMATED manner, RELIABLY, FREE OF CHARGE and EFFICIENTLY.
fields.PURPOSE: Signatures must still be capable of validation years later – hence the duty extending beyond the validity period.
fields.DEADLINE: at any time, without time limit beyond the validity period
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Annex I · Annex I – qualified certificates for electronic signatures Ten mandatory items (a) to (j): machine-readable indication that the certificate is a qualified certificate, a data set on the issuing QTSP including its Member State of establishment, name OR pseudonym of the signatory, signature validation data, period of validity, unique identity code, advanced electronic signature or advanced electronic seal of the QTSP, the location, free of charge, of the underlying certificate, an indication of the certificate validity status service and an indication whether a QSCD is used. Article 32(1) · The eight verification points of QES validation The validation confirms validity only where all eight conditions are met: a qualified certificate complying with Annex I at the time of signing, issuance by a QTSP and validity, correspondence of the validation data, correct provision of the data set representing the signatory, clear indication of any pseudonym, creation by a QSCD, integrity of the signed data and fulfilment of Article 26. Point (f) – the QSCD condition – is precisely the point that is missing in Article 32a. Article 34 · Qualified preservation service Requires procedures and technologies capable of extending the trustworthiness of a qualified signature beyond its technological validity period. Cryptography ages – without preservation a 15-year-old signature loses its evidentiary value. To be distinguished from Article 45j: preservation keeps the SIGNATURE alive, archiving keeps the DOCUMENT alive.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Is the OCSP/CRL service free of charge, highly available AND also capable of being queried for expired certificates?
fields.KEY POINT: Five properties: at any time, beyond the validity period, automated, reliable, free of charge.

fields.CONTENT: Paragraph 4a: Paragraphs 3 and 4 SHALL APPLY ACCORDINGLY to the revocation of QUALIFIED ELECTRONIC ATTESTATIONS OF ATTRIBUTES. Paragraph 4b: The Commission shall be empowered to adopt DELEGATED acts in accordance with Article 47 establishing ADDITIONAL measures referred to in paragraph 2, point (fa).
fields.PURPOSE: The QEAA follows the certificate regime; risk management can be deepened by way of a delegated act.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 45d(4) · Finality of revocation Provides that a revoked qualified electronic attestation of attributes is no longer valid from the moment of its revocation and shall not in any circumstances regain validity. Article 24(2) · Catalogue of QTSP obligations The central catalogue, in practice the structure of every audit: (a) notification duties (one month for changes, three months for cessation), (b) qualified and trained staff in accordance with European or international standards, (c) sufficient financial resources or liability insurance, (d) pre-contractual information, (e) trustworthy systems including suitable cryptographic techniques, (f) verifiable data storage, (fa) risk management, (fb) 24-hour notification, (g) protection against forgery and data loss, (h) recording duty extending beyond the cessation of activities, (i) termination plan, (k) certificate database. Point (j) was deleted – the gap is intentional. Article 47 · Exercise of the delegation Governs the procedure for delegated acts: the duration of the delegation, revocation at any time by the Parliament or the Council, the consultation of experts and the objection period within which the Parliament or the Council may raise objections. The Regulation refers to Article 47 in only three places: Article 5c(8), Article 24(4b) and Article 30(4).
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Note: paragraph 4b is a DELEGATED act (Article 47), not an implementing act.
fields.KEY POINT: QEAAs inherit the revocation regime of certificates.

fields.TOPIC: Implementing act on the requirements of paragraph 2
fields.CONTENT: Implementing act with a list of reference standards and, where necessary, specifications and procedures for the requirements referred to in paragraph 2. Where those are complied with, the PRESUMPTION OF CONFORMITY applies for that paragraph.
fields.PURPOSE: Together with the implementing act under Article 20(4), this implementing act is the most important audit document for QTSPs.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: ETSI EN 319 401 · General requirements for trust service providers The base standard of every trust service audit. It deals, among other things, with risk assessment, the practice statement and terms and conditions, organisation and reliability of staff, facility and access security, operational and network security, incident management, records, business continuity and the termination of the service. Relationship to eIDAS: gives concrete form to Article 24(2), points (b), (e), (fa), (g), (h) and (i) eIDAS as well as to Article 19a(1), point (a) eIDAS. Through the formula 'European or international standards' in point (b) it is at the same time the bridge to ISO/IEC 27001. ● Summary of content, not verified against the original text Relevance here: gives concrete form to points (b) and (fa); through the formula 'European or international standards' it is the point of attachment for ISO/IEC 27001. Article 24(2) · Catalogue of QTSP obligations The central catalogue, in practice the structure of every audit: (a) notification duties (one month for changes, three months for cessation), (b) qualified and trained staff in accordance with European or international standards, (c) sufficient financial resources or liability insurance, (d) pre-contractual information, (e) trustworthy systems including suitable cryptographic techniques, (f) verifiable data storage, (fa) risk management, (fb) 24-hour notification, (g) protection against forgery and data loss, (h) recording duty extending beyond the cessation of activities, (i) termination plan, (k) certificate database. Point (j) was deleted – the gap is intentional. Article 48(2) · Examination procedure Refers to Article 5 of the Comitology Regulation (EU) No 182/2011. A committee composed of representatives of the Member States delivers an opinion by qualified majority; where the opinion is negative, the Commission may not adopt the draft. All implementing acts under this Regulation follow this procedure.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Which version of the QTSP requirements implementing act is taken as the basis in the audit?
fields.KEY POINT: Article 24(5) + Article 20(4) = the audit double pack.

fields.TOPIC: EU-wide recognition of qualified trust services
fields.CONTENT: Qualified services issued or provided in ONE Member State SHALL BE RECOGNISED as such IN ALL OTHER Member States: (1) QES and qualified electronic seals based on qualified certificates; (2) certified QSCDs and qualified electronic seal creation devices; (3) qualified certificates for electronic signatures/seals as well as qualified trust services for the management of remote qualified electronic signature creation devices and remote qualified electronic seal creation devices; (4) qualified validation services; (5) qualified preservation services; (6) qualified electronic time stamps; (7) qualified certificates for website authentication; (8) qualified ERDS; (9) qualified EAA; (10) qualified electronic archiving services; (11) qualified electronic ledgers.
fields.PURPOSE: Without automatic EU-wide recognition, qualified status would be limited nationally – Article 24a is the table of contents of all eleven types of qualified service.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 22 · Trusted lists Obliges each Member State to establish, maintain and publish lists of the qualified providers and their qualified services – in a secured manner, electronically signed or sealed and in a form suitable for automated processing. The information on the body responsible for the list, the place of publication and the certificates used for signing is to be notified to the Commission without undue delay, which in turn makes it available in a secured form suitable for automated processing. Article 14 · International aspects Governs the recognition of trust services from third countries or from international organisations as legally equivalent, provided that an implementing act or an agreement pursuant to Article 218 TFEU exists. The act or the agreement must ensure that the requirements applicable to Union providers are complied with and that the third country maintains its own trusted list. Agreements must in addition secure reciprocity.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Is a qualified service from another Member State being refused? That would be an infringement of Article 24a.
fields.KEY POINT: LEARNING TIP: Article 24a(1)-(11) is the complete list of all types of qualified service. Ideal for learning by heart.

fields.TOPIC: Prohibition of discrimination for electronic signatures
fields.CONTENT: An electronic signature SHALL NOT BE DENIED legal effect and admissibility as EVIDENCE in legal proceedings SOLELY ON THE GROUNDS that it is in an electronic form or that it does not meet the requirements for QES.
fields.PURPOSE: Without this basic rule a court could reject any simple signature across the board – the entire signature hierarchy would be worthless.
fields.CROSS-REFERENCES: Article 35(1) · Prohibition of discrimination for seals Prohibits denying an electronic seal legal effect and admissibility as evidence solely on the grounds that it is in an electronic form or that it does not meet the requirements for qualified electronic seals. Article 41(1) · Prohibition of discrimination for time stamps Prohibits denying an electronic time stamp legal effect and admissibility as evidence solely on the grounds that it is in an electronic form or that it does not meet the requirements of the qualified electronic time stamp. Article 43(1) · Prohibition of discrimination for registered delivery services Prohibits denying data sent electronically legal effect and admissibility as evidence solely on the grounds that they are in an electronic form or that they do not meet the requirements of the qualified electronic registered delivery service. Article 45b(1) · Prohibition of discrimination for attestations of attributes Prohibits denying an electronic attestation of attributes legal effect and admissibility as evidence on the sole ground that it is in electronic form or that it does not meet the requirements for qualified attestations. Article 45i(1) · Prohibition of discrimination for archived data Prohibits denying electronically archived data and documents legal effect and admissibility as evidence on the sole ground that they are in electronic form or that they do not meet the requirements for qualified electronic archiving services. Article 45k(1) · Prohibition of discrimination for ledgers Prohibits denying an electronic ledger legal effect and admissibility as evidence solely on the grounds that it is in an electronic form or that it does not meet the requirements for qualified electronic ledgers. Article 46 · Legal effects of electronic documents The whole of Chapter IV consists of this single article with one sentence: an electronic document shall not be denied legal effect and admissibility as evidence in legal proceedings solely on the grounds that it is in electronic form.
fields.AUDIT CHECK: Not relevant to the audit, but central in procedural law: the assessment of evidence remains free, only blanket rejection is prohibited.
fields.KEY POINT: 'Not solely on the grounds' – the prohibition of discrimination runs as paragraph 1 through SEVEN articles.
